YoLM9EatW2s.title: Nvidia Can't Buy Enough of It. I Found 2 Ways In
YoLM9EatW2s.summary: Brian argues memory — not electricity, as Elon Musk claims — is the true scarce input in the AI buildout, evidenced by Nvidia's gross margin slipping to 75% (guided to 72-73%) as COGS doubled to $63B, and its 'supply and capacity' commitments footnote jumping from $119B to $279B, primarily for memory and manufacturing. His method: compare each company's last four quarters of gross margin against the prior four — margin only rises when you own something scarce. Across 24 companies tested, 13 passed. Vertiv passes (+4.3 points on +26% revenue, deferred revenue doubling to $3.6B) but gains little pricing power; nVent fails (margin -2.2 points on +46% revenue — a commodity). SanDisk, spun from Western Digital 18 months ago, is the cleanest pass: gross margin from 26% to 85%, +41.4 points with revenue nearly tripling. Micron is the headline: same-quarter margin from 37.7% to 84.6% (+35.4 points), ~6x next-year earnings, with 16 long-term supply agreements to 2030 and customers getting only 50-67% of requested supply — though the market may be pricing a repeat of the 2018 peak-to-bust cycle. The real risk is China: a state-backed memory maker's $8.6B July IPO, now starting ~9 wafers for every 10 Micron starts, with Apple testing its chips and US senators pushing back. Constellation Energy (+24.5 points) is the honest electricity trade (already-built, licensed reactors), but he hasn't done valuation work on it — not a recommendation. Calls: SNDK BUY; MU BUY; VTI UNCERTAIN; NVT AVOID; CEG UNCERTAIN. Sponsored segment for CopperOne Resources.

Personal AI agents launching across 3B+ users could monetize via take rates — but must be sticky versus Anthropic, OpenAI, Grok, and Gemini. (published 2026-09-30) is a dip-buy call: Lowe's (LOW, BUY at $189) with relatively HIGH conviction. His DCF fair value is $241, implying ~27% upside over 12–18 months. Beyond the call: the thesis is classic cyclical mean-reversion — revenue stagnated as pandemic-era demand was pulled forward (the 2020 home-improvement boom created a "reckoning" as repaint/remodel cycles stretched), compounded by shrinking disposable income (non-substitutable inflation in food, rent, insurance, healthcare) and management guiding flat-to-low-single-digit 2026 growth, with the stock down >20% in 2026 while the market rose double digits. The moat argument: home improvement is a ~$1T annual category that doesn't disappear — delayed projects eventually get done, and growth should re-accelerate to mid-to-high single digits once the economy normalizes. Margin pressure is the key risk: operating margin fell to 11.3% from over 15% in 2023, driven by wage inflation (McDonald's $20/hr California example feeding up the wage ladder); management's AI initiatives will improve profits only incrementally. Valuation hook: forward PE of 14.5, the lowest in several years. No other tickers called; Home Depot not mentioned. Sponsored by The Motley Fool. x_VEI4OnjaU.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc delivers his final verdict on Micron after the company reported what he calls fantastic quarterly results, concluding a four-part deep dive. The centerpiece is management guidance: NAND bit shipments growing mid-20% in 2027 and 2028 with the industry supply-constrained in both years, and DRAM growing low-20% with the same constraint — meaning shortages for Micron's core memory and storage products likely persist through 2028 and possibly into 2029, with management unable to see when supply/demand balances. Micron is raising 2027 capex to accelerate space availability for 2028+. Parkevtate argues the capex is strategically calibrated (overbuilding would hand competitors an opening; he likens it to poker bluffing dynamics from his pro-poker past). On valuation, he notes two straight quarters of 80%+ operating margins with the next expected the same, yet the stock trades at just 5.8x forward P/E — about one-fifth of the S&P 500 average — proof the market treats Micron as a cyclical peak-earnings business. His DCF fair value is $1,439 vs ~$1,097 market price. Verdict: MU — BUY, high conviction (a flip from his UNCERTAIN stance on Oct 5). Bull: shortages hold and ASPs stay elevated. Bear: the cycle turns and earnings compress.

-PP31UU49TA.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc explains why October's University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading matters for stock investors. Sentiment fell 1.8 points from September's 48.1 to roughly 46, below the 47.3 expected, driven by frustration over the cost of living. His framework splits inflation into substitutable categories (beef, where buyers can switch to chicken or pork) and non-substitutable ones, where the pain concentrates: food overall +2.7% over 12 months, gasoline +27%, fuel oil +52%, utility gas +4.4%, shelter +3%, hospital services +5.2% and vehicle maintenance +5.2%. Motor-vehicle insurance (-5.1%) is the rare relief, though he expects elevated repair costs to push premiums back up. Because lower- and middle-income households spend a larger share of income on these essentials, sentiment is depressed even with unemployment near 4% and employers hesitant to fire. For stocks, he expects discretionary categories - travel, autos, dining, theme parks - to feel the pinch as consumers trade down to store brands and smaller pack sizes, a pattern he says is already visible at Walmart, Costco, Procter & Gamble, Pepsi and Coca-Cola, slowing sales, profits and hiring. He is not turning bearish while layoffs stay limited, but sees no near-term catalyst for living costs to fall. No explicit stock call in this video.

His scenarios: bear €240 (-37% on shrinking EPS), base €470 (+25%, ~10%/yr, 7% EPS growth), bull over 50% upside; his buy limit is €340 and sell zone ~€490, and he concludes you could definitely build a position here in a solid, broadly diversified luxury group, though he is not invested yet. Call: CONDITIONAL_BUY.

Z5gI10nu3Pk.title: Dan Ives: The AI Boom Is Only 15% Over—Here's What Comes Next  | Top Stocks
Z5gI10nu3Pk.creator: MarketBeat
Z5gI10nu3Pk.summary: Collaboration between Top Stocks (Matt Weinschenk, Stansberry) and MarketBeat (host Bridget Bennett), recorded at the Stansberry conference in Las Vegas, interviewing Dan Ives — formerly Wedbush, now Yorkville Ives and Company — on the state of the AI bull market. Ives argues the AI party started at 9:30pm, is now at about 11:30pm and runs to roughly 4am: investors are, in his view, less than 15% through the coming AI spending, with an $8–10 multiplier across tech for every $1 spent on an Nvidia chip, and 2–3 more years of tech bull market. On AI safety and possible slowdowns, he says technology always outruns regulation, self-regulation is the likely path, and slowing down hands the lead to China; safety itself is a growth area (cybersecurity, sovereign AI). He discusses Palantir and Nvidia on sovereign AI, Meta's Muse assistant and 3.5B-user install base, hyperscaler monetisation inflecting (Microsoft/Azure, Google, Amazon), neo-clouds Nebius and CoreWeave (auto-captions garble Nebius as 'Navitas' and IREN as 'Iron'), Tesla's 6–9 month robotaxi/Optimus pivot and a >80% chance of a Tesla–SpaceX merger by end-2027, Apple's new AI strategy and 2027 anniversary iPhone, AMD as a huge player under Lisa Su, and software winners/losers (Salesforce and ServiceNow must prove themselves; Adobe and Intuit face AI headwinds). The hosts note Apple and Microsoft sit in Ives's top-10 stocks to buy, but Ives states no explicit buy/hold/sell call, price or target for any ticker in the interview — all ticker entries are logged UNCERTAIN. Caption spots are garbled in places (names above; 'Turnus' for Apple's incoming CEO Ternus).

YNdllTBJmJ0.title: Should You Buy Meta Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
YNdllTBJmJ0.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
YNdllTBJmJ0.summary: Parkev Tatavosianc previews Meta Platforms ahead of its quarterly results after the close on Wednesday 21 October, a stock he has ranked as his best, then second-best, buy of the year and holds himself. He notes Meta Muse, its new personal agent, reached 5 million downloads faster than ChatGPT or Anthropic, and that the shares have recovered from about $550 to $734, up over 11.75% in 2026. The core case rests on the last quarter: revenue up 28% to $60.8 billion, ad impressions up 14% and price per ad up 12%, with 3.6 billion daily users — evidence, in his view, that AI spending is improving engagement rather than just adding ad load, even though operating income fell 8% to $18.8 billion and headcount fell 1%. He expects Q3 revenue near or above the $61–64 billion guide, helped by midterm-election ad spending, and expects the 2026 capex guide of $130–145 billion to be raised on component costs rather than extra capacity. His call is META — BUY at $734 (stated), ranked #2 best buy, with a DCF fair value of $914, about 24% upside over 12–18 months; he advises buying before earnings if you own none, splitting the purchase 75/25 or 50/50. No stance flip (was BUY).

J-OmpNfuFX0.title: PepsiCo Stock: A Dividend King at a 10-Year Low?
J-OmpNfuFX0.creator: The German Value Investor
J-OmpNfuFX0.summary: The German Value Investor examines PepsiCo, a 54-year dividend grower now yielding nearly 5% after falling about 35% since 2023 to $126 — back at its 2019 price level, with a market cap of about $172 billion. He argues the apparent cheapness (headline P/E about 16) is misleading: since 2013 revenue has risen from $66 billion to about $94 billion while net income only moved from under $7 billion to about $8 billion, margins have shrunk below 9%, and recent growth came from price rises rather than volume. PepsiCo even cut snack prices about 15% in early 2026 to defend volume, which he reads as a weakening moat. The latest quarter's 17% profit jump flatters one-off comparisons; core growth was only about 2%, and management cut its core growth forecast on 8 October from 5–7% to 2.5–3.5%. Free cash flow of roughly $5.5 billion over three quarters is more than paid out in dividends and buybacks, while net debt is about $40 billion and refinancing will cost more; US Treasuries yielding over 5% look safer by comparison. His valuation puts a normal-scenario fair price near $80 with a buy limit around $56. His call is PEP — SELL at $126 (stated), suggesting holders consider selling. First tracked call on PEP, no flip.

k1xJbNAGmFg.title: This Hasn’t Happened Since 2006!
k1xJbNAGmFg.creator: BWB - Business With Brian
k1xJbNAGmFg.summary: Brian (Business With Brian) argues US profits are growing faster than higher interest rates can pull prices down — the first time this setup has appeared since 2006 — even though the 10-year yield is at its highest since 2002 and the week's fall was much rougher under the surface: the S&P 500 slipped about 1% while chip stocks fell about 9%. Since June, expected S&P profits are up about 10% against prices up about 3.5%, and 72 companies guided above forecasts, the most since FactSet tracking began in 2006. He filters for five AI hardware names down more than 9% in the week whose profits are expected to grow at least 15% next year with forecasts raised since July, warning they swing two to three times harder than the market on rate-spike days, so positions should be staged and the riskiest kept extremely small. Vertiv (garbled as 'Verdive' in auto-captions) is the worked example: EPS up about 60%, outlook raised, stock down about 31% since July. All five calls are CONDITIONAL_BUY, each conditional on waiting for imminent earnings and then dollar-cost averaging small: VRT (signal 'buy a lot'; wait for 28 October earnings), NVT, ONTO, FIX and INOD (the riskiest, very small only). VRT softens his prior BUY; NVT, ONTO, FIX and INOD are first tracked.

fH5DacZxQug.title: I Put $10,000 Into 5 Stocks During This Selloff. Here’s Why
fH5DacZxQug.creator: Couch Investor
fH5DacZxQug.summary: Couch Investor reviews a bruising week in which his cash portfolio fell 11.6% against the S&P 500's roughly 2% fall, argues the selloff is not justified, and walks through buy zones ahead of a heavy earnings week — Netflix on Tuesday 20 October and Meta on Wednesday, alongside Tesla, IBM, Lam Research and Texas Instruments. He notes 84% of S&P names are already at least 10% below their highs and, with the index near 20x forward earnings, rejects the dotcom-bubble comparison. He discloses putting $10,000 into five stocks during the selloff and details four explicit buys: AVGO — BUY at about $328, position up 10%, buy zone $315–335; RKLB — BUY at about $50, raised by 3.7% (plus an earlier 25 shares at $61–62), despite Neutron testing now running into early 2027 and a possible Q2 2027 launch; AXON — BUY at $409, position up 15%, back at its original entry floor after a round trip to $600; and NBIS — BUY at about $165, bought twice in 10-share lots above the current price, buy zone $160–172, which he calls best-in-class and a future $100B+ company. Other names are buy-zone commentary only: GOOGL $330–342, SOFI, AMZN about $250, META $660–690, CRWV about $61 and AMD $510–540. A Peter Lynch clip on having the stomach for corrections closes the video. NBIS flips CONDITIONAL_BUY to BUY; the others reiterate prior BUYs.

SzdxupnhTfY.title: The AI Sell Off is HERE   3 Stocks to BUY the DIP on
SzdxupnhTfY.creator: Mark Roussin CPA
SzdxupnhTfY.summary: Mark Roussin's weekly playbook argues the AI selloff, compounded by hot inflation data — CPI at 3.7% and PPI up 6.3% year on year — is a buying opportunity, and reads the falling 10-year Treasury yield during the selloff as a defensive rotation into safety rather than simple rate relief: consumer staples, healthcare and energy led the past month while AI and semiconductors took the selling. He stresses investors now ask what companies will earn from AI spending, not just how much is spent, so selectivity matters. Using FastGraphs (the video's sponsor), he features three dip buys. VRT — BUY, first tracked: Vertiv's power, cooling and liquid-cooling for AI data centres, earnings expected up 36% next year, PEG under 1, health score about 80 and net debt/EBITDA of 0.2, with roughly 30–40% upside on his multiples; the bear case is exposure to any AI capex slowdown. NVDA — BUY, reiterated: about 10% off highs at 13.5x next-year earnings, with $315 possible by the end of Q1 next year at 20x, on the full platform and CUDA moat; bear case is capex-ROI questions and custom-chip competition. AVGO — BUY, reiterated, added at the end of last week: custom AI chips and networking, revenue up 86%, AI semiconductor revenue up 220% and record free cash flow at about 17x forward; bear case is meaningful debt. He also briefly discloses recently adding AMD — BUY, flipping his 13 October CONDITIONAL_BUY to BUY.

XOmt1qanNWc.title: Interesting News for Netflix Stock Investors | NFLX STock Analysis
XOmt1qanNWc.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
XOmt1qanNWc.summary: Parkev Tatavosianc analyses Netflix's announcement that it will cut 6% of its workforce, roughly 1,000 employees — its largest reduction since 2022 — across product, HR, technology and legal. He reads the move, set out in an email from co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters, not as cost-cutting but as a reallocation toward AI-related hiring in content creation and productivity, noting Netflix will keep investing aggressively in high-impact areas without growing overall headcount. He supports that reading with revenue per employee above $3 million, up from about $2 million in 2017, which he says shows no bloating. The timing matters: Netflix reports earnings after the close on Tuesday 20 October, and it is the largest position in his portfolio. The bear side he acknowledges is engagement: growth was only low-single-digits in the first half of 2026 and in 2025, so Netflix is losing viewing share to short-form rivals such as TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, and investors were unconvinced by management's acquisition and pricing answers. The shares are also well down since the Warner Bros bid episode, from which Netflix stepped back. His call is NFLX — BUY at $69.72 (stated), reiterated, with fair value implying about 65% upside over 12–18 months (about $115), a forward P/E of 18.5 he calls the cheapest in years, and interest in adding if it stays at these levels. No flip.

WZIfLpuA3eo.title: Hims Is Reaching 3 Million Member Milestone
WZIfLpuA3eo.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
WZIfLpuA3eo.summary: Parkev Tatavosianc reviews Hims & Hers as a potential high-upside disruptor in a healthcare industry he argues is ripe for disruption because customers are unhappy with incumbents — the opposite, he says, of payments, where Visa and Mastercard users are broadly satisfied. The growth numbers are strong: revenue up 40% to $753 million in the quarter, about 300,000 net new members taking the total close to 3 million, and international revenue up 17x year on year to $131 million after the Eucalyptus acquisition; management guides long term to $6.5 billion of revenue and $1.3 billion of adjusted EBITDA, against $2.6 billion of trailing revenue. The problems are profitability and returns: operating margin has fallen to 0.3% from about 8% a couple of years ago, and return on invested capital has reversed from about 35% in early 2025 to −8.4%, even though operating cash flow has stayed positive for multiple quarters. His discounted cash flow value is $26.90 against a market price of about $26 — a 3% gap he calls fairly valued — at a forward P/E of 37.6. His call is HIMS — CONDITIONAL_BUY: he reiterates his 14 September 'buying opportunity, medium conviction' rating but is waiting for a more attractive entry point, expecting the stock's volatility to offer one. First tracked Parkev call on HIMS, no flip.

vBt4asdgxoI.title: Great News for Taiwan Semiconductor Stock Investors | TSM Earnings Analysis
vBt4asdgxoI.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
vBt4asdgxoI.summary: Parkev Tatavosianc reviews Taiwan Semiconductor's Q3 2026 earnings: revenue $47B, up 41% year on year, with gross margins over 66% and operating margins approaching the high-50s, both above the high end of guidance. Leading-edge nodes are ramping fast — 2nm rose from 3% to 8% of wafer revenue in one quarter and 3nm is 33% — while high-performance computing (AI) reached 68% of revenue as smartphone share fell to 21% because handset makers order less as component prices rise. TSMC reiterated 2026 capex of $60–64B against sold-out capacity and customer deposits booked through 2027 into 2028, but again guided long-term gross margins down as new technology and overseas fabs ramp. The stock fell 1.8% on the print despite being up over 40% in 2026; at $422, 18.8x forward earnings, Parkev reiterates his BUY with high conviction against a $584 DCF fair value, flagging China/Taiwan geopolitics and a possible AI slowdown as the main risks.

3m_ctu3RWcc.title: Affirm is Appreciated By Consumers and Merchants as it Facilitates Sales
3m_ctu3RWcc.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
3m_ctu3RWcc.summary: Parkev Tatavosianc revisits Affirm, the buy-now-pay-later lender, after interest rates moved higher. Revenue has grown from $250M in 2020 to $4B over the trailing 12 months, operating-cash-flow-to-sales is at a record high, and revenue per employee has nearly tripled to $1.7M, helped by AI. He argues consumer balance sheets are healthy — unlike before the financial crisis, the excess borrowing this cycle sits with governments, which is where his macro concern lies. On valuation, Affirm at $74 and 14.8x forward earnings looks slightly undervalued overall, though his DCF fair value of $73.16 says fairly valued. He reiterates his late-August BUY ranking but downgrades conviction from medium to low because the valuation is less attractive and rates and macro conditions have worsened.

7-mrCZ8hZ-E.title: Netflix Stock Down 46% Despite Record Profits. Why?
7-mrCZ8hZ-E.creator: The German Value Investor
7-mrCZ8hZ-E.summary: The German Value Investor asks why Netflix is down 46% from its June 2025 all-time high despite record profits — nearly $12B of net income in the last 12 months, a ~25% net margin, ROE around 50% and strongly positive free cash flow, almost all returned via buybacks. He walks through the growth fade (revenue growth back to 16% after a 6–7% trough), viewing share slipping to YouTube, and a margin ceiling as operating leverage runs out. His scenarios: negative (3% then 1% growth, fair P/E 11) implies ~50% downside; normal (14% then 9%) gives a fair price around $80; positive (17% then 11%) puts fair value ~50% higher. Verdict: a HOLD at $72 with an expected return of ~8% — fairly valued, no bargain; his buy limit is $53 and his community-portfolio position is a small ~1%.

v7HZ3VIPa3E.title: 4 AI Stocks to Buy After the Market Sell-Off!
v7HZ3VIPa3E.creator: Couch Investor
v7HZ3VIPa3E.summary: A Motley Fool collaboration in which Neil (Couch Investor) and the Motley Fool host each present two quality AI buys after the market sell-off, favouring well-capitalised, cash-generating names over debt-reliant ones. Neil picks Nebius — best-in-class AI cloud, ex-Yandex team, revenue guided from $1.3B toward $23B by FY28, deliberately holding capacity back to rent megawatts at premium prices — and Broadcom, the 'anti-Nvidia' custom-silicon play at ~$340 and ~20x forward earnings, with AI revenue guided to double to $115B then ~$230B. The co-host picks Lumentum and Coherent, the optical-interconnect names benefiting as AI clusters hit the 'copper wall', both capacity-constrained into 2028–29 with Nvidia backing.

tNp6Mj3v_1k.title: This ‘Always’ Happens to Stocks in a Midterm Year (It’s Happening Again Now)
tNp6Mj3v_1k.creator: MarketBeat
tNp6Mj3v_1k.summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews Mark Chaikin of Chaikin Analytics on the midterm-year pattern and the current AI-led pullback. Chaikin argues, from 100 years and 24 midterm cycles, that markets typically bottom in mid-October in a midterm year and then rally, with a median gain of about 22% to the following summer peak, so pullbacks on AI-scare or geopolitical headlines are buying opportunities rather than a reason to exit. He says software has turned after its January-to-July collapse and features three software buys: Palantir, a defence, government and enterprise data disruptor pulled back from a high and stabilising, which he wants to own for the next 6–12 months ahead of 2 November earnings; ServiceNow, breaking out to a six-month high after an upgrade, consolidating workflow and customer support; and CrowdStrike, down a little over 10% in a week after roughly doubling year to date, as AI and agentic software expand the cyber threat surface. His favourite stock for 2027 is AMD, now down 18% in a week — a flip from his earlier conditional stance to an outright BUY, citing its 64-bit floating-point chip for scientific and medical research and PC processors overtaking Intel. No prices or targets were stated for any call. Passing mentions included Dell, HPE, Micron, CoreWeave, Adobe, Salesforce, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet.

8DCwORvros4.title: Anthropic Delivers Fantastic News for AI Stock Investors | NVDA, MRVL, INTC, AMD, AMZN, AVGO, GOOG
8DCwORvros4.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
8DCwORvros4.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA reacts to Anthropic's reported third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, up roughly 50% quarter on quarter from about $11.5 billion in Q2, implying a run rate near $67 billion, and discusses an expected IPO valuation around $2 trillion, possibly around November, which he frames as reasonable in comparison with SpaceX. His central argument is ecosystem-wide rather than stock-specific: Anthropic's growth is good news for the AI and semiconductor supply chain that provides its compute. The tickers discussed in that context are Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle, TSMC, ASML, Broadcom and Marvell, alongside Intel in the title — all logged as UNCERTAIN passing mentions, with no explicit buy, hold or sell call, no stated price and no fair-value estimate for any of them. The caveat he returns to is demand quality: he wants to see proven end-customer use cases delivering a positive return on investment, rather than spending justified only by the build-out itself. He attributes recent semiconductor weakness to interest-rate and government-debt fears rather than to a break in the AI story. The video was first seen as members-only and later became public, which is why it was analyzed in the 15:00 run.

psF8L-jn5aI.title: AI Stocks Are Falling. Dan Ives Says It’s Just Getting Started.
psF8L-jn5aI.creator: MarketBeat
psF8L-jn5aI.summary: MarketBeat, partnering with Matt Weinschenk from Top Stocks, interviews Dan Ives on the state of the AI bull market — the same interview previously posted on 16 October and analyzed as video Z5gI10nu3Pk, republished here under a new title as AI stocks fall. Ives argues the AI party started at 9:30pm, is now at about 11:30pm and runs to roughly 4am: investors are, in his view, less than 15% through the coming AI spending, with an $8–10 multiplier across tech for every $1 spent on an Nvidia chip, and two to three more years of tech bull market. On AI safety and possible slowdowns he says technology always outruns regulation, self-regulation is the likely path, and slowing down hands the lead to China; safety itself is a growth area, including cybersecurity and sovereign AI. He discusses Palantir and Nvidia on sovereign AI, Meta's Muse assistant and its 3.5 billion-user install base, hyperscaler monetisation inflecting at Microsoft, Google and Amazon, neo-clouds Nebius and CoreWeave, Tesla's six-to-nine-month robotaxi and Optimus pivot and a more-than-80% chance of a Tesla–SpaceX merger by end-2027, Apple's new AI strategy, and AMD as a major player under Lisa Su. The hosts note Apple and Microsoft sit in Ives's top-10 stocks to buy, but Ives states no explicit buy, hold or sell call, price or target for any ticker in the interview, so all entries are logged UNCERTAIN and no stance flip is recorded. Auto-captions garble several names, including Nebius, Palantir and Ives himself.

4BooxjnAfPY.title: This Stock Is Undervalued
4BooxjnAfPY.creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
4BooxjnAfPY.summary: Joseph Carlson previews the second week of earnings season — SpaceX, Netflix, Meta, Tesla and Moody's all report — against growing AI-bubble concern, then criticises Brad Gerstner for talking bullish on TV while cutting Altimeter's exposure to its lowest in three years, and names ESPN (Disney) fail of the week over its embrace of gambling sponsorships. On SpaceX he is positive on the company (Starlink connectivity best, +65%) but at a $2.56T cap vs $12B trailing revenue he prefers Amazon ($775B revenue, AWS alone $148B) — SPCX and AMZN UNCERTAIN. Netflix is his 8th-largest holding: at 19x forward earnings he holds his full position into earnings with cautious optimism, argues the engagement-problem narrative misreads the Warner Bros bid, watch-time reporting and the 6% layoffs (whose memo reaffirmed full-year guidance), and sees a rerating to ~25x — NFLX HOLD, a BUY→HOLD change from his 5 Oct add with the bullish thesis intact. Meta is a HOLD through the capex cycle on monetisation power (ad price +12%, impressions +14%, ad revenue +27%). Tesla is an AVOID at 154x forward earnings on flat fundamentals and a slow robotaxi rollout. The undervalued stock of the title is Moody's: one of the best companies in the market and 'a particularly strong investment' right now — MCO BUY (first tracked). ASML is a passing analogy (bought sub-$700 after its 2025 narrative selloff) — UNCERTAIN.

VLlqZqAsvRI.title: 4 Stocks You’ll Wish You Bought Before Earnings
VLlqZqAsvRI.creator: Couch Investor
VLlqZqAsvRI.summary: Couch Investor previews a pivotal earnings season (Netflix, Tesla, Meta this week; Amazon, Google, Intel, Reddit, Robinhood, SoFi and PayPal next) and picks four names he calls fairly cheap before they report. Sea Limited is first tracked here — BUY: down 31% year to date, forward P/E 21.1x, revenue growing near 35-40% and repeatedly beating revenue expectations, though free cash flow is flat and EPS misses. Alphabet is a BUY reiterated at about $343: Google Cloud grew 81.8% with expanding margins and could approach 100% growth, while heavy capex keeps free cash flow negative. Voyager Technologies is a CONDITIONAL_BUY: a small position he holds, halved from its highs at a $1.53 billion cap, unprofitable to about FY28, so the case rests entirely on execution against a huge defence/space TAM. Nebius is a BUY reiterated at $162 — he bought more last week; revenue is expected to scale from $1.3 billion towards $23 billion by FY28 as GPU spot prices rise. He closes by saying inclusion does not oblige anyone to buy before the print.

Ilnv_YwsbX0.title: Roblox Excercises Conservative Revenue Recognition Policy
Ilnv_YwsbX0.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
Ilnv_YwsbX0.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA revisits Roblox after a $10-12 rise since his 31 July buy call. The title's point is accounting: Roblox spreads Robux deposits over 12-24 months while users spend them in days, so reported revenue is understated and losses overstated; on price to free cash flow (21x, near multi-year lows) he calls it undervalued, while his updated DCF of about $46 against $49.55 says fairly valued and just inside his margin of safety. Cost cuts doubled cash flow from operations to sales (15% to 37%) and revenue per employee rose to $1.76 million. He reiterates BUY, medium conviction — first tracked in this watch, no prior tracked stance.

hIg3gx2OmnM.title: Monster Beverage Is Gaining Market Share in the Energy Drink Category
hIg3gx2OmnM.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
hIg3gx2OmnM.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA asks whether Monster Beverage's 20% revenue growth and US/international share gains make it a buy. Revenue has tripled since 2017 to $9.2 billion and ROIC has recovered to 26%, but operating margin has compressed from 38% to 29%, forward P/E 34.6 sits near its high, and his raised DCF of just over $37 remains below the $45+ price — slightly overvalued. He reiterates HOLD (his 1 July stance; first tracked): not a buy here, not worth dumping either. He closes by naming Celsius the better buying opportunity in the category — CELH BUY reiterated as a side mention.

W942c9Uw8aw.title: Here's What I'm Planning With My Eli Lilly Position
W942c9Uw8aw.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
W942c9Uw8aw.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA checks his Eli Lilly position: revenue has more than doubled since 2023 to $79.7 billion on weight-loss injectables, the pill version is gaining adoption, operating margin is 49.7% with gross margin above 80%, and ROIC recently near 40% is about four times WACC. At a forward P/E of 26 and his updated DCF of $1,523 against $1,251, he sees more than 20% upside over 12-18 months. He reiterates BUY with relatively high conviction and wants to add rather than take profits; US drug-price pressure is the named headwind. Videos first seen as members-only and later public, hence analyzed in this run.

OJRRAUXcQzI.title: The Stock Market Is About to Make a BIG Move
OJRRAUXcQzI.creator: Mark Roussin CPA
OJRRAUXcQzI.summary: Mark Roussin CPA argues the market may be setting up for a big move: fear is at 23 (extreme fear), midterms are weeks away and the S&P 500 has returned positively in the 12 months after every midterm since 1950 (about +15% on average), tech has pulled back 10-20% while earnings and cash flow still climb, and a possible end to the Iran war could lower oil, inflation and Fed hike pressure (three hikes are priced by end-2027; he expects fewer). He is selective — backlog and real AI earnings over borrowed-money build-outs — naming Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD and Marvell as producing real earnings today and CoreWeave and Oracle as not high-quality and not in his portfolio. No explicit buy, hold or sell call, price or target for any ticker, so all six are logged UNCERTAIN and the video does not alert on its own.

FFArRRXrliA.title: 3 Stocks to Buy Before Midterms (Get PAID No Matter Who Wins)
FFArRRXrliA.creator: MarketBeat
FFArRRXrliA.summary: MarketBeat interviews Mark Lichtenfeld (The Oxford Club) in Savannah on getting paid whatever the midterm outcome: do not invest on polls, stay the course if long-term, and own dividend payers across three sectors. Financials: Lincoln National (LNC) — BUY, insurers gain as rates rise, annuity demand, de-risked via reinsurance, 4.5% yield. Healthcare: AbbVie (ABBV) — BUY, long-time favourite, perpetual dividend raiser, Q2 revenue +10%, ~18x earnings. Energy: Phillips 66 (PSX) — BUY, his favourite refiner; Hormuz risk premium keeps oil elevated and Wall Street's expected 2027 earnings decline looks too pessimistic. All three are first tracked MarketBeat calls; no flips, no share prices stated.

IhtkjAPaBrA.title: I'm Buying More Of This Stock Tomorrow
IhtkjAPaBrA.creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
IhtkjAPaBrA.summary: Joseph Carlson devotes most of this episode to Netflix's Q3 earnings, reported the previous day, because NFLX is a large position in his portfolio (he says he is up about $15,000 on it). He argues the numbers are far stronger than the narrative: stripping out the one-off Warner Bros Discovery payout, Netflix just posted record normalized free cash flow of $2.9 billion, trailing buybacks of about $12.9 billion are genuinely reducing the share count, and underlying EPS growth is roughly 20% a year rather than stalling as headline charts suggest. The real problem is growth optics and engagement: revenue growth is decelerating from 16% in 2025 toward about 10.9% expected in 2027, and the Wall Street Journal is highlighting flat Netflix viewing against YouTube's climb. Carlson rebuts the YouTube thesis directly — churn fell year on year in Q3, so viewers are adding YouTube without cancelling Netflix. He reads the firing of roughly 1,000 staff including content chief Bela Bajaria, and the hiring of Peter Rice (Fox/FX pedigree: The Bear, Shogun), plus talks with Warner's Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy, as a deliberate pivot from algorithm-driven volume to prestige, must-see content. At a forward P/E of about 18 and a free cash flow yield near 4%, he sees limited downside and large upside if content quality improves, and the title states he is buying more tomorrow — a flip from his HOLD of 20 Oct. He also covers SpaceX's blowout quarter (revenue roughly $7B to $14.5B, Starlink subscribers 12M to 13.6M) with no explicit call, praises Intuitive Surgical's quarter (not yet invested, deep dive planned), and closes with a 'fail of the week' attacking AI bear Ed Zitron's motives. Caption note: a personal name in the Zitron segment was redacted in the caption file; figures are as spoken in auto-captions.

7jcAqx7huGU.title: Market Volatility Is Back — Here’s How to Profit in 15 Minutes
7jcAqx7huGU.creator: MarketBeat
7jcAqx7huGU.summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews Kareem and Brian of Monument Traders Alliance on profiting from rising volatility with two paired strategies. Brian (short-term, technicals) runs a 'dark ticker' trade: if IWM, GLD or QQQ closes down 1% or more, buy calls in the 4:00-4:15pm ET window after the close, hold 1-2 days and sell on the next-day rebound — IWM CONDITIONAL_BUY, QQQ CONDITIONAL_BUY, GLD also traded this way. Kareem (longer-term, fundamentals) argues gold is a hedge against US debt over $40T and currency debasement: GLD BUY reiterated (keep buying, dollar-cost average), AEM BUY (Agnico Eagle, premier miner, margins expand as gold rises), and NUV BUY (Nuveen muni closed-end fund, 4.73% tax-free, 6.14% taxable-equivalent at 30%, buy at current levels near its 52-week low and keep adding). Suggested split for a hands-off investor: about 90% in safer appreciating assets and 10% in the short-term trading strategy. No stance flips; GLD was already BUY on 2026-10-06, the other four are first tracked MarketBeat calls.

LVPcoXodNNA.title: Massive News for Salesforce Stock Investors | CRM Stock Analysis
LVPcoXodNNA.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
LVPcoXodNNA.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA reacts to Salesforce agreeing to buy AI marketing platform Braze for almost $5.7 billion in enterprise value, paying $47.50 per share — a premium of over 30% — with the deal expected to close in fiscal 2028. He likes that Salesforce will pay cash rather than issuing stock, which he reads as a signal management does not view its own shares as overvalued, but he stresses Salesforce's poor capital-allocation record: it has repeatedly overpaid for acquisitions, and return on invested capital is only 12.74% at a record high, barely above its cost of capital and below 10% for most of the past decade, among the lowest for peers of its size. The stock fell about 2.7% on the news. He updates his discounted cash flow model slightly higher on expected free cash flow to a fair value of $276 per share versus a $240 market price, and notes a forward P/E of 14.95, near late-2023 lows. Call made: CRM — BUY at $240 stated (DCF $276), reiterated from 2026-09-25, but conviction downgraded from high to medium (change dated 20 Oct) because the price has risen and macro dynamics have worsened. Base case is that Salesforce stays embedded in enterprise operations and is not significantly disrupted by agentic AI.

X4iwiPHULtQ.title: Should You Buy Alphabet Stock Before the Huge Investor Update? | GOOG Stock Analysis
X4iwiPHULtQ.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
X4iwiPHULtQ.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA previews Alphabet ahead of its huge investor update on 28 Oct, which he will cover live for members. He owns the stock and reviews the last quarter reported 22 July: revenue up 24%, Google Services up 15% to $94.5 billion, Google Cloud up 82% to $24.8 billion, operating income up 30% at a 34% margin. He warns investors have become complacent about LLM disruption to Search, contrasts Alphabet hiring about 12,000 more staff year-on-year with Meta cutting 1%, and focuses on cash flow: operations generated $39 billion against $44.9 billion of capex, a negative free cash flow of about $5.9 billion, funded in part by roughly $90 billion of equity issuance he opposes. He urges Alphabet to sell its SpaceX stake, which he calls ridiculously overvalued, instead of diluting holders — that SpaceX comment is a passing opinion (SPCX — UNCERTAIN), not a call on SpaceX itself. Gemini processes 22 billion API tokens a minute with 950 million monthly users, across six other billion-user products. His updated DCF is $373 versus a $346 market price, forward P/E 22. Call made: GOOGL — CONDITIONAL_BUY at $346 stated (DCF $373), high conviction long term, but do not buy before the 28 Oct update — he sees more downside than upside into the print and advises holders who want to add to wait until after results.

n2uLj3gmL4I.title: Why Is BigBear.ai Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | BBAI Stock Analysis
n2uLj3gmL4I.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
n2uLj3gmL4I.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA re-rates BigBear.ai in a video dated 19 Oct 2026, after the stock has fallen almost 61% year-to-date to $2.11, and asks whether it is finally a buying opportunity. He has warned against it all year and says the answer is still no. Revenue has fallen from a $160 million trailing peak to $132 million after Department of Government Efficiency cuts delayed, paused or cut government contracts, and the company has failed to expand into enterprise the way Palantir did. Margins have deteriorated sharply: cash flow from operations to sales is at a record low of -54% after management spent on acquisitions to try to revive growth. The balance sheet still holds $321 million in cash and short-term investments raised during the earlier retail frenzy, so no capital raise is needed soon, but continued losses make dilution eventual. Forward price-to-sales has fallen from over 25 to 6.3, yet he argues the business was in better shape in January 2025. He revises his free-cash-flow estimates lower — worse than even his bearish prior view — to a DCF fair value of $1.90 versus $2.11 market, fairly valued to slightly overvalued. Call made: BBAI — AVOID at $2.11 stated (DCF $1.90), first tracked stance; it is getting closer, but needs a price fall or a revenue and cash-flow turnaround first.

o3L-3ZDKjcg.title: I'm Investing $20,000 Into These 2 Stocks
o3L-3ZDKjcg.creator: Mark Roussin CPA
o3L-3ZDKjcg.summary: Mark Roussin CPA says he is putting nearly $20,000 to work in two long-term growth stocks, but he is not buying either at market — instead he is selling December 18 cash-secured puts to get paid to wait for his entry prices, targeting over $1,200 in combined premium on about $19,500 of backing cash. For Rocket Lab he likes the integrated space business beyond Electron launch — space systems, spacecraft components and satellite systems — with Q2 revenue of about $234 million up roughly 62% and a $2.4 billion backlog, while flagging that the Neutron rocket's first launch has been delayed to 2027 and the name remains speculative. For Credo Technology he focuses on high-speed connectivity and active electrical cables for AI data centres, with fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of about $480 million up roughly 115%, 68% non-GAAP gross margin and full-year guidance for over 85% growth, balanced against concentration risk — its top four customers are about 84% of revenue — and he already owns shares. Calls made: RKLB — CONDITIONAL_BUY, entry only via the Dec 18 $45 put at about $2.40 premium (effective basis $42.60), first tracked call; CRDO — CONDITIONAL_BUY, entry only via the Dec 18 $150 put at about $9.90 premium (effective basis $140.10), a soft flip from BUY on 2026-10-13 back to his 8 Oct put stance.

8aRHUhVcSqQ.title: Every Midterm Since 1946 Ended the Same Way
8aRHUhVcSqQ.creator: BWB - Business With Brian
8aRHUhVcSqQ.summary: BWB - Business With Brian walks through 80 years of midterm-election market history, covering every midterm since 1946 ahead of the 3 November vote, and stresses this is not a political video. He makes four points. First, a midterm year — year two of a president's term — is historically the weakest of the four for the S&P 500, averaging about a 5% gain, with a drop of at least 10% at some point in about two of three years, driven by uncertainty; this year has been gentler, with a biggest dip of about 9%. Second, in all 20 midterms since 1946 the S&P 500 was higher a year after election day, up about 14% on average, and usually already higher within three months. Third, a flip of the House or Senate did not break that pattern; the expected setup — a Republican president losing the House — last occurred in 2018, when the market fell about 15% into Christmas Eve before finishing up about 12% a year later. Fourth, tech and the Nasdaq have beaten the S&P in the year after 11 of 13 midterms, by almost twice as much on average, but also dip harder into the vote. He explicitly says this is not a reason to load up on tech before the vote, and that earnings and interest rates will matter more than the election. No stock calls are made in this video.

wQWYpGDT6Q4.title: My Favorite Stocks Are a Screaming Buy Today
wQWYpGDT6Q4.creator: Couch Investor
wQWYpGDT6Q4.summary: Couch Investor frames his favorite stocks as a screaming buy after headline-driven market jitters over the Middle East hit growth, semiconductor and AI names harder than defensives. Most of the video is Meta's quarter reported Wednesday after the close: revenue up 26% to $64 billion, ad impressions up 10%, price per ad up 14%, daily active people up 3%, and extensive detail on the Muse personal agent — over 10 million people set it up in about six weeks in the US and Canada, with monetisation planned sooner than usual through fees, subscriptions and ads. He notes this was Meta's first quarter since 2012 with no free cash flow as capex doubled, and discusses the planned Class C non-voting share dividend on 19 January. He then covers Sundar Pichai podcast comments on Alphabet — Gemini 4, capacity planned years ahead still short, Cloud forgoing revenue to feed frontier models — and models Nebius (auto-captions garble it as Nebuse/Nebs) 2027 exit ARR at $28 billion conservative, $33 billion base and $40 billion bull against a roughly $40-43 billion market cap, plus a new $3.5 billion Citi facility. Calls made: META — BUY under $700 stated (will add if it goes lower); GOOGL — BUY, no price stated (overlooked, very big winner); NBIS — BUY at a ~$40-43B market cap stated, no share price (severely undervalued on his scenarios); SPCX — UNCERTAIN, passing mention only via Google's capacity leasing. No stance flips — all three BUYs reiterate prior BUYs.

jgCqtS02Rr0.title: 4 Stocks You’ll Wish You Bought on This Dip (One Is Down Over 50%)
jgCqtS02Rr0.creator: MarketBeat
jgCqtS02Rr0.summary: MarketBeat host Bridget talks buy-the-dip ideas with guest Alec Green, chief investment strategist at the Oxford Club. Green sees a concentrated market (top 8 S&P names >35% of the index) leaving overlooked mid/large and international names cheap despite strong earnings, with the post-midterm 'midterm miracle' seasonality (~+19.5% average over the following 9 months) as a near-term catalyst. His four picks: MercadoLibre (MELI), Novo Nordisk (NVO, recently re-added at under 10x earnings), Tyler Technologies (TYL) and speculative Summit Therapeutics (SMMT, FDA decision due mid-November).

BJnxdy-y4Xc.title: AI Stocks Are the Most Hated Trade Right Now. The Numbers Say Otherwise
BJnxdy-y4Xc.creator: Couch Investor
BJnxdy-y4Xc.summary: Couch Investor argues the AI selloff is a sentiment move, not broken fundamentals. He opens with Peter Lynch clips on having the stomach for drawdowns and not needing near-term money in stocks, then notes the chip index (SOX) is down 26.7% and names like Nebius, Lam Research and Applied Materials are near 50% off their highs, even though the sector keeps beating expectations: TSMC revenue up 41.2% with Q4 guidance up 58%, Nvidia data-centre revenue more than doubled last quarter, and Broadcom AI revenue up 221% with guidance to roughly double twice to $230B. He flags Meta turning free-cash-flow negative on capex, and the roughly $2.3T of contracted demand as a risk if OpenAI and Anthropic cannot fund their commitments, with Oracle the most indebted of the group. Historically the SOX has taken about 54 calendar days to rebound; he also cites Tom Lee calling the selloff near its end. Nebius is his poster-child neocloud, planning 1GW of Vera Rubin capacity in 2027. He makes no explicit ticker call: long-term holders may find opportunities now, but waiting for next week's Fed meeting and earnings is also fine. Captions garble some names (Nebius, Anthropic) and one hedge-fund statistic.

GOeiq0K6kP4.title: Cava Reported Revenue Increasing by 31%
GOeiq0K6kP4.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
GOeiq0K6kP4.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Cava Group is an undervalued restaurant opportunity after a strong quarter. Cava's revenue rose 31% year over year, with 17 new restaurants taking the estate to 476 locations and same-store sales up 9%, driven by 5.3% traffic growth, so part of the growth is organic rather than just new openings. Trailing sales have climbed from roughly $500M in 2023 to about $1.37B, and he sees a long runway from under 500 Mediterranean locations toward 3,000-6,000 at maturity, in a market crowded with pizza, burger and burrito concepts. The problem is profitability: operating cash-flow margin has flatlined around 16% since 2025 as tariffs, oil and input costs lifted both opening and operating costs, and returns on invested capital, once approaching 15% and ahead of early-stage Chipotle, have stopped improving. He updated his discounted cash flow and revised estimates slightly higher, putting fair value at about $52 against a market price a little over $58, so even after a margin of safety the shares look slightly overvalued. The call is CAVA — HOLD, low conviction, his first tracked Cava call; he is watching for margin improvement to resume while revenue keeps expanding. One forward price-to-sales figure is garbled in the auto-captions.

ITH0wVU__UI.title: I'm Buying More
ITH0wVU__UI.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
ITH0wVU__UI.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reviews Netflix's Q3 results as a shareholder — Netflix is the largest position in his portfolio — after the shares fell more than 4.5% on the day and over 30% overall. Investor focus sits on engagement growing only in low single digits and an advertising rollout that is behind its aggressive target, with partner-integration delays. Management also cut its 2026 free-cash-flow guide from $12.5B to $12B. Against that, he stresses the core content engine (Stranger Things, Squid Game, Bridgerton), roughly 95% of spending on the core business, a record 31.7% operating margin, and licensing deals such as Disney and Globo content already lifting engagement, plus hints of a possible future free ad-supported tier. He reads management's outlook as pointing to strong 2027 revenue growth, with formal guidance expected on the Q4 call. He cut his fair value by about $4 a share after the print (the exact new figure drops out of the auto-captions) but still calls the stock roughly 75% undervalued, says he is more bullish than before, and is likely to add toward his roughly 20% maximum portfolio allocation before Q4 results. The call is NFLX — BUY reiterated, no stance flip.

uXWXsaBWMgU.title: Should You Buy Amazon Stock Before the Massive Investor Update? | AMZN Stock Analysis
uXWXsaBWMgU.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
uXWXsaBWMgU.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc previews Amazon's Q3 results, due after the close on 29 October, from the perspective of a shareholder who ranks Amazon among his ten best stocks and wants to add. The setup is AWS: it accelerated to 37% year-over-year growth last quarter, up from 28%, on quarterly revenue above $200B (up 20%) and operating income of $27.5B, with trailing operating cash flow of $161B. Free cash flow is nonetheless negative $7.6B on data-centre capex. His test for the print is precise: AWS growth above 39% would be positive, anything below 37% a disappointment given the capacity being added. Supporting points include a chips business above a $25B run rate growing at triple digits, 30-40% better price-performance from Graviton processors, and unpriced upside from Amazon's Anthropic stake. His discounted cash flow is $317, about 20% upside over 12-18 months. To manage the binary earnings risk he suggests new buyers split 50% before and 50% after the results, and existing holders 25% before and 75% after. The call is AMZN — BUY reiterated at a $317 DCF, no stance flip.

R8zyCTNiP5c.title: Interesting News for eBay Stock Investors
R8zyCTNiP5c.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
R8zyCTNiP5c.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc updates eBay after the company announced a 9% headcount reduction, its second round of cuts this year after 6% earlier, to streamline operations and prioritise its best units. He links the cuts to AI letting companies do more with fewer staff, macro caution over consumer spending after tariffs and higher oil prices, and duplicate roles after eBay's acquisition of secondhand-fashion marketplace Depop. eBay has been one of his better 2026 picks, up over 41% year to date plus dividends, on an asset-light marketplace model that owns no inventory or logistics and throws off significant free cash flow, even if the platform itself has seen little improvement and revenue growth is solid rather than explosive. That run has pushed the forward price-to-earnings ratio to 18.4, the highest in a couple of years, and his updated discounted cash flow values the business at about $110 a share against a $123 trading price, so it now looks slightly overvalued after a margin of safety. He therefore downgrades eBay from a buying opportunity, last updated 24 August 2026, to a hold at medium conviction. The call is EBAY — HOLD at $123 with a $110 DCF, his first tracked eBay call, so no formal tracked flip.

9EjvFSLy_Eo.title: Why Is DigitalOcean Stock Falling and is it a Buying Opportunity?
9EjvFSLy_Eo.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
9EjvFSLy_Eo.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks why DigitalOcean stock is falling despite accelerating growth, and whether the drop is a buying opportunity. Management is guiding fourth-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 35%, up from 28% in the most recent quarter, and at least 50% growth in 2027, but says that growth will come at the expense of operating profit margins as it invests in capacity. He traces revenue from about $300 million in 2021 to $1 billion over the trailing twelve months, crediting agentic AI and the shift from closed to open-weight models, with customers value-maxing rather than token-maxing. The cost is margin: cash flow from operations has fallen to 31% of sales from a 39% peak, which makes investors treat the growth as investment-driven rather than organic. The shares are still up over 111% year to date but down from about $180 to about $102. He likes R&D leverage — 18.7% of revenue, down from 29% in 2022 — and a forward P/E of 55 against 50% forecast growth. His updated discounted cash flow is $122 a share against about $102, roughly 20% upside over 12 to 18 months. Having called it too expensive on 13 May, he now upgrades it. The call is DOCN — BUY at a $122 DCF, his first tracked DigitalOcean call.

jFBWQkDC_1o.title: Macroeconomic Headwinds are Hitting Clorox From All Sides | CLX Stock Analysis
jFBWQkDC_1o.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
jFBWQkDC_1o.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reviews a very difficult fiscal 2026 for Clorox and asks whether investors should run away or buy the dip. Net sales fell 5% as value-conscious consumers traded down to cheaper unbranded and store-brand products, a trend he says Clorox, Kimberly-Clark, Procter & Gamble and retailers from Walmart to Amazon all report. At the same time tariffs and the war in Iran lifted input costs, and the CEO resigned for health reasons with a replacement still being sought. Sales have fallen from a $7.5 billion pandemic peak, when disinfectant wipes surged, to $6.7 billion, operating margin is around 13% against 18 to 20% normally, and revenue per employee has dropped from over $900,000 to $800,000; he would not be surprised by a major restructuring with large job cuts. The stock is down 13.4% in 2026, from near $130 to a low near $80 and back to about $87, trading at a forward P/E of 14.25, near multi-year lows. He revised his free-cash-flow estimates slightly lower, putting fair value at $100 against $87. The call is CLX — BUY reiterated, but conviction cut from medium to low. One operating-margin figure drops out of the auto-captions.

LauJrBZP3xc.title: Is SpaceX Stock a Buy After Reporting Spectacular Earnings Results?
LauJrBZP3xc.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
LauJrBZP3xc.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc works through SpaceX's latest results and asks whether spectacular earnings make the stock a buy. Revenue rose 161% to $14.6 billion and operating income swung to a $2.8 billion profit from losses a year earlier. The fastest growth came from the superintelligence segment, up to $7.56 billion from $813 million, because SpaceX rented its computing power to customers including Alphabet and Anthropic instead of using it for its own AI model, which he ranks only fourth or fifth behind OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini; that makes it more like CoreWeave, which commands a lower valuation premium. He calls Starlink the sustainably attractive segment: subscribers nearly doubled to 13.6 million, connectivity revenue reached $5.2 billion and operating income $2.4 billion, a margin above 40%. Against that, capital spending is enormous — $48 billion in the first nine months of 2026 against $13.1 billion of operating cash flow — and the stock trades at 63 times price-to-sales, near its cheapest on that measure but still rich, with a large Elon Musk premium embedded. The call is SPCX — HOLD, low conviction: exciting, but he would wait for a better entry point. Several segment figures are partly garbled in the auto-captions.

MCLfOaku5MA.title: He Got Rich Off AMD at $2. He's Buying These Stocks Next.
MCLfOaku5MA.creator: MarketBeat
MCLfOaku5MA.summary: MarketBeat interviews Matt McCall of Monument Traders Alliance, who made his name buying AMD at $2 and now pitches five beaten-down high-growth names for the next AI wave, arguing money will rotate from mega-caps toward mid and small caps. His blue-chip robotics pick is Teradyne (TER), where semiconductor testing drives growth of roughly 130% in earnings in 2026 and robotics and cobots are cheap upside at a double or triple bottom. Grail (GRAL) is his high-risk play: its Galleri blood test screens for more than 50 cancers, FDA approval is expected in early 2027 and Medicare coverage would be the bigger catalyst, with 10-bagger or takeover potential. Kratos Defense (KTOS) is a future-of-warfare hedge in unmanned aircraft, with a rising defence budget and a return to fair value worth a double. FormFactor (FORM) is picks-and-shovels for quantum — cryogenic testing is needed whoever wins — profitable at about 20% growth, a P/E in the low 20s and a PEG near 1. Fabrinet (FN) covers AI photonics and optics for data centres, down about 11% over a year despite earnings. All five are buys on pullbacks, with no share prices stated and all first tracked for MarketBeat.

qHzoSWzT92I.title: Should You Buy SoFi Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
qHzoSWzT92I.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
qHzoSWzT92I.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc previews SoFi's investor update and earnings on Tuesday 27 October and answers whether to buy before the print. He raises his fair value from $19 to $19.82 a share against a stated market price of $14.82, about 34% upside over 12 to 18 months at a forward P/E of 18.5. The most recent reported quarter showed revenue up 43% to $1.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 44%, members up 35% year over year to 15.8 million and loan originations of $14.8 billion, helped by a digital-only model without legacy branch costs. The bull case is the technology platform: accounts fell 16% year over year to 135 million after losing a large client, though they rose 2 million in the quarter, and a return to growth there could earn SoFi a technology rather than a bank valuation. The bear case is rates: higher and faster-rising rates could cut the fair value of the $46.6 billion loan book by several billions and lower loan-sale prices, and macro, oil and inflation headwinds worsened in the quarter being reported. The call is SOFI — CONDITIONAL_BUY: long-term bullish, but he would not buy before the update, with an optional 25% before and 75% after route he personally would not use.

O7T5j4MCaXA.title: What's Going on With Meta Stock?
O7T5j4MCaXA.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
O7T5j4MCaXA.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc recaps Meta's earnings reaction and asks what is going on with the stock. Meta beat on both the top and bottom line and gave a reasonably exciting forecast, yet the shares rose 4 to 5% during his members-only live earnings coverage and then fell 6 to 7% the following morning as he recorded. Much of the video recaps the traction of Muse, Meta's personal agent: about 10 million people set it up in roughly a month and a half, around 25% use it daily, and shopping is the top use case so far. He stresses Meta's distribution advantage — its family of apps can put a new agent in front of billions of users quickly — and the early monetisation routes he discussed in the live session, including transactions, subscriptions and business use. He promises a deeper dive into the conference call in the next few days, including management's spending and AI plans. Crucially, he states no valuation, fair value or buy, sell or hold view in this short recap, so it is recorded as commentary only. The call is META — UNCERTAIN, no price stated; his prior Parkevtate META BUY from 18 October stands and there is no stance flip.

_CtOnOGIRtc.title: 2 MUST OWN ETFs as Tech Stocks CRASH
_CtOnOGIRtc.creator: Mark Roussin CPA
_CtOnOGIRtc.summary: Mark Roussin frames a tech sell-off driven by AI-spending, inflation and Federal Reserve worries — the Nasdaq-100 down more than 6% in two weeks and the S&P 500 down about 2% on his stated figures — and previews a heavy week: the Fed meeting on 27–28 October, PCE inflation data and roughly 180 earnings reports. His answer is to complement a tech-heavy portfolio with two dividend ETFs he calls must-own. SCHD, the Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF, is a top-five holding, up 27% year to date against the S&P's 11% on his figures, yielding about 3% with 14 consecutive years of dividend growth, a 0.06% expense ratio and roughly 100 holdings screened on cash flow, profitability and dividend growth rather than yield alone. HDV, the iShares Core High Dividend ETF, is the higher-yield, more defensive second name: up 24% year to date, a yield above 3%, 0.08% fees and about 80 holdings tilted to staples, energy, healthcare and utilities — the four sectors that led the past month — with technology only about 1%. He cautions that the two overlap (both hold Chevron, Procter & Gamble and Verizon) and that HDV's top ten are 55% of the fund. The calls are SCHD — BUY reiterated and HDV — BUY, first tracked.

TXQ8h7gfyMY.title: I Bought $10,000 of These Stocks Ahead of Earnings. Here's Why
TXQ8h7gfyMY.creator: Couch Investor
TXQ8h7gfyMY.summary: Couch Investor reviews a rough stretch — his portfolio down 1.42% on the week and 14.2% on the month, though still up 25.1% year to date against the S&P 500's 11.45% — and walks through buy zones for his book ahead of what he calls the mother of all earnings weeks, with SoFi, PayPal, Robinhood, Alphabet, Microsoft, ServiceNow, Intel, Amazon, SanDisk and Reddit all reporting. He plays clips from Nebius and from Amazon/AWS arguing that AI capacity is sold out for 2026 and largely for 2027, then discloses $10,000 of dip-buying: ten extra Nebius shares at $160 into his largest position, ten Nvidia shares (a 30% position increase) because it is cheap, five Alphabet shares at the $320 close (up 3.8%), still inside a buying zone capped at $342, and three Meta shares at $642 (up 5.2%), inside his main $630–$645 zone with resistance at $663 then $700-plus. He also thinks Google Cloud could grow about 100% year over year this quarter, while expecting Alphabet's free cash flow to stay negative on capex. The long technical-analysis section gives buy zones for many other names (Rocket Lab, SoFi, Amazon, Nu, Netflix, Reddit, Axon, MercadoLibre, Uber, Broadcom, CoreWeave, AMD and others) without trades, so only the four disclosed buys are recorded as calls: NBIS, NVDA, GOOGL and META — all BUY reiterated.

l81JZUo8WzI.title: Down 98%, Is it Finally Time to Buy Chargepoint Stock? | CHPT Stock Analysis
l81JZUo8WzI.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
l81JZUo8WzI.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc revisits ChargePoint after a fall of more than 98% over five years and asks whether it is finally time to buy, against a backdrop of higher oil prices and faster EV adoption outside the United States (he notes the US is only 6 of 100 new EV buyers). The operating story has genuinely improved: revenue is recovering to $433 million on a trailing basis with another growth quarter forecast, management has stopped growing at any cost, the latest quarter was essentially cash-flat, and operating cash flow relative to sales has improved from minus 65% to minus 16%. The balance sheet is the problem: cash has dwindled from over $600 million to just over $95 million against more than $227 million of debt — more than the market capitalisation — so any return to the old burn rate would force dilutive raises or expensive borrowing. His discounted cash flow, which only reaches free-cash-flow break-even in fiscal 2028 and positive territory from fiscal 2029, still leaves the stock overvalued at the stated $8 price (up 11% on the day) even after a margin of safety; the fair-value figure itself is garbled in the auto-captions, rendered as '$529' where $5.29 fits the pattern of dropped decimals. The call is CHPT — AVOID, reiterating a warning he has given for over five years, though he says it is getting closer.

-WLGFBndtqg.title: 3 AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy Before Earnings!
-WLGFBndtqg.creator: Couch Investor
-WLGFBndtqg.summary: In this collaboration (byline 'The Motley Fool and 2 more'; the scan's earlier shelf listing carried the title 'Nebius vs. CoreWeave: Which AI Stock Wins the SpaceX Boom?'), Couch Investor and Neil argue SpaceX's earnings were very bullish for the whole AI infrastructure industry. SpaceX ended the quarter near 1.7 gigawatts, is closer to 2 gigawatts now and targets about 2.5 by year-end, then roughly 13 gigawatts next year — at about $50 billion per gigawatt that implies over half a trillion dollars of spending, against a guided 2027 exit revenue range of $500 billion to $1 trillion on a $100 billion exit ARR this year, with payback periods under a year and possibly six months. They doubt the hyperscalers will stand still and let SpaceX take the compute. Neil's neocloud pick is Nebius: a $40–45 billion company, SemiAnalysis platinum-ranked, ex-Yandex engineering depth, Nvidia as investor, Microsoft and Meta contracts, and Vera Rubin capacity coming online in 2027. Couch likes Nebius but says he does not own it here; his own pick is CoreWeave — also platinum-ranked, 1.5 gigawatts of active power, moving into higher-margin enterprise work — with future funding costs the key earnings question. The bear case is neocloud debt and build-out speed. The calls are CRWV — BUY (Couch's pick, first explicit) and NBIS — UNCERTAIN for Couch (Neil's pick). A few figures drop out of the auto-captions, including the Vera Rubin gigawatt figure.

QNci5DHflos.title: Why Is Everyone Talking About Meta Stock?
QNci5DHflos.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
QNci5DHflos.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc explains why so many investors are talking about Meta: the Muse personal agent. It has grown to over 10 million users in roughly its first month and a half, and management told his members-only earnings live session that it could prove even more lucrative per user than a typical social-media user, where Zuckerberg already cites average revenue per American user in the several hundreds of dollars a year. Average transaction value through the agent is already around $200. Monetisation is still being built: commerce tools that pay Meta a fee on each transaction the agent facilitates, and subscriptions for the most advanced models or extra tokens. The agent is expensive to run, but Meta is building capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years and expects compute cost efficiency to improve tenfold within a year — roughly a 90% cost reduction — which he finds plausible given distribution across Facebook, Instagram and the other apps with several billion daily users. His back-of-the-envelope maths: 200 million US and Canada users at about $200 of average revenue each would be $40 billion a year before any global rollout. As a shareholder he is optimistic, but he states no valuation, fair value or buy, sell or hold ranking in this video. The call is META — UNCERTAIN, commentary only; his earlier BUY stands.

hdlnj5H42vw.title: Massive Update for Nebius Stock Investors | NBIS STock Analysis
hdlnj5H42vw.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
hdlnj5H42vw.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc upgrades Nebius in this video — a stance flip. On 14 October he had ranked it a hold, low conviction, at over $209 a share (he also cites a $198.60 high that day), warning it still was not a buying opportunity; with the shares now slightly below $160 he upgrades it to a buying opportunity, dating the change 23 October 2026 in the video, for high-risk-tolerance investors only. Forward price-to-sales has compressed from over six a few months ago and over five a few weeks ago to 3.553. The industry backdrop still favours suppliers: lease pricing is rising from $10–15 million per megawatt toward $40 million, and memory, GPU, power and permitting constraints keep supply scarce, though he flags the real long-term risk — contracts of one to six years may not renew if the industry is oversupplied by then. Nebius carries about $10 billion of long-term debt against $51 billion at one competitor. A 20–30 basis-point fall in interest rates lifted his discounted cash flow because so much of the value sits years out; the fair-value figure itself drops out of the auto-captions, but he says that at a current price of about $160 Nebius is now significantly undervalued. He also says the stock is down about 35% since his ranking, though $209 to $160 is nearer 23% on his own figures. Amazon and Alphabet report on 28–29 October. The call is NBIS — BUY, flipped from HOLD.

HtJpT1AHqQw.title: Should You Buy Microsoft Stock Before the Huge Investor Update? | MSFT Stock Analysis
HtJpT1AHqQw.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
HtJpT1AHqQw.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc previews Microsoft's earnings, due after the close on 28 October 2026, and answers whether to buy before the update. He owns the stock — added around $400 in February after a fall to near $350 — ranked it an excellent buying opportunity earlier this year, then downgraded it to a hold a couple of weeks ago (last evaluated 5 October) as the valuation richened; at $524 he reiterates that hold: not a seller, but not a buyer before the print either, because elevated event risk needs a higher prospective return. His updated discounted cash flow is $447 against the $524 price — slightly overvalued — while the forward P/E of 22.1 is below the stock's own average. The most recent quarter (reported 29 July) showed revenue of $90 billion, up 18% year over year, with the AI segment growing over 40%; his earnings-growth estimate of about 20% sits above the analyst figure, which drops out of the auto-captions. His watch list: Microsoft 365 paid seats (30 million stated), progress on its own chips, where it trails Alphabet and Amazon, a backlog approaching $500 billion (the unit drops out of the captions) and its OpenAI concentration, fiscal 2027 capex, and whether Microsoft stays the only hyperscaler that is free-cash-flow positive. The call is MSFT — HOLD reiterated.

zVc-S0Od8_0.title: Nvidia Just Gave Away the Next Boom (THIS IS HUGE!)
zVc-S0Od8_0.creator: BWB - Business With Brian
zVc-S0Od8_0.summary: Brian frames AI as a brain and its reflexes: Nvidia now reports data center (the brain) separately from edge computing (the reflexes in PCs, cars and robots), and he argues both win because every device reflex sends more work back to the brain — with the brain growing about four times faster today and the reflexes set to become the bigger business in the early to mid-2030s. After mid-October's chip sell-off (the longest losing streak since 2008, about $2 trillion gone), his signal ladder puts Nvidia at severely undervalued at about 23 times next year's earnings, with data-center revenue of about $89 billion in a quarter; he dollar-cost averages down. Broadcom is undervalued (slightly undervalued after risk adjustment, given its up-to-$71 billion financing for one customer). Micron is off his ladder for lack of a trusted valuation, SanDisk sits in his reassess-the-business tier, Qualcomm and ARM are slightly overvalued to fairly valued at about 100 times earnings, Ambarella is fairly valued pending a growth re-acceleration, Tesla is fairly valued on outside estimates, Alphabet is fairly valued with good news priced in, and Amazon is slightly undervalued but he wants this week's earnings first. A sponsored Greenland Mines segment is not recorded as a call. Calls: NVDA and AVGO — BUY; AMZN and AMBA — CONDITIONAL_BUY; GOOGL — HOLD, flipped from BUY; TSLA — HOLD; MU, SNDK, QCOM and ARM — UNCERTAIN.

4MK0MfxbOHw.title: 3 Growth Stocks Under $20 With 100%+ Upside
4MK0MfxbOHw.creator: MarketBeat
4MK0MfxbOHw.summary: MarketBeat's host interviews Kristen Orman, director of research at the Oxford Club, whose method is to screen thousands of US-listed stocks for a strong story plus a concrete dated catalyst, growing revenue and earnings, lower debt and high beta. Almonty Industries (ALM; the auto-captions garble the name repeatedly) is restarting the Sangdong tungsten mine in South Korea — cheaper than a new build, with founder-CEO Lewis Black heavily invested; it trades under $10 after a fall of about 36% in a month, analysts see about 170% upside, and the catalysts are a design-capacity update within about 60 days and US restrictions on Chinese tungsten from 1 January. Kopin (KOPN; captions render 'Copen') makes micro-displays for military helmets and drones, has just won an $18 million contract ($34 million total) against a market cap just under $660 million, and could double in 12–18 months, with a January CES presentation as the catalyst. Cullinan Therapeutics (CGEM; captions render 'CGM') is a pre-revenue biotech with autoimmune data due around December and a partnered lung-cancer FDA action date of 27 February, trading near $15 against a $33 analyst consensus. All three are BUY, first tracked.

B7qSvzcSMNc.title: I'll Buy or Sell SoFi After Earnings. Here's What Decides It
B7qSvzcSMNc.creator: Couch Investor
B7qSvzcSMNc.summary: Couch Investor previews SoFi's Q3 report, due Tuesday 27 October before the market opens, and sets out exactly what would make him buy more.
