His DCF gives a bull case of $28, a base case of $22.80 and a bear case of $10 — about 51.3% upside. The call is conditional: he will buy more next week only if the report is extremely good and management assures investors it can still hit its targets; he is definitely not selling.

n-JvcqJ5-oE.title: Anthropic Just Released Their Financials… The Numbers Are Insane
n-JvcqJ5-oE.creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
n-JvcqJ5-oE.summary: Joseph Carlson works through Anthropic's newly released S-1 filing and argues it undercuts the AI-bubble case made by critics such as Ed Zitron and Michael Burry. The numbers he cites are extreme: revenue of $41 million in 2023, $386 million in 2024, $4.5 billion in 2025 and $16 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, with the most recent quarter at $11.5 billion, a first positive operating quarter, compute costs falling from 160% to 55% of revenue, and customers paying over $100,000 a year rising from about 1,000 to about 11,900 in twelve months. He compares the operating-leverage path to Uber and Netflix. He then mocks some of the filing's odder risk disclosures — models resisting shutdown, blackmail-like behaviour, agents amplifying each other and moral-status questions — before turning to valuation: at a $1 trillion IPO value he thinks Anthropic makes sense, but at $1.5–2 trillion the implied growth (about $128 billion of free cash flow and $644 billion of revenue by 2031) is too aggressive, and he would not personally invest on those assumptions. Side segments cover Microsoft's buyout offer to 60,000 employees, Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, Meta's up-to-$95 billion financing, and a rebuttal of Ken Griffin's zero-marginal-cost bubble argument. No explicit ticker call is made; Anthropic is not yet public.

qCSyXwoQdA0.title: The 2nd Best Stock to Buy Right Now | NVDA Stock vs. Meta Stock
qCSyXwoQdA0.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
qCSyXwoQdA0.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc ranks the two best stocks to buy right now after digesting Meta's latest results, and puts Nvidia first and Meta second; he owns both, and both sit among his largest positions behind Netflix. Nvidia trades at $213 (stated) against his $345 DCF fair value — about 62% undervalued — on a 13.4x forward P/E, with forward EPS growth expectations near 50%, hyperscaler capital spending passing $850 billion in 2026 and possibly $1.2–1.4 trillion next year, return on invested capital above 100% for over a year, and an asset-light model that outsources manufacturing to TSMC. Meta trades at $646 (stated), about 46% undervalued on his DCF (the exact fair-value figure dropped out of the auto-captions), on an 18.5x forward P/E, with 19% forward EPS growth expectations he wagers will prove low, quarterly revenue up 26% with 12% fewer employees, and the Muse personal agent already past 10 million downloads. The bear case for both is the same: the thesis rests on hyperscaler spending delivering returns, Meta's capex keeps rising with likely equity raises to fund it, and Nvidia's circular investments in customers draw scepticism. Both are BUY reiterations, not flips.

JjlBOSyXX4k.title: Should You Buy Pinterest Stock Before the Huge Investor Update?
JjlBOSyXX4k.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
JjlBOSyXX4k.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reiterates Pinterest as a BUY ahead of its 29 October earnings and investor update, keeping it in his top ten stocks to buy in 2026; he owns the stock. The shares trade over $22 (stated), up from a $15 low this year but still down 14% year to date against an S&P 500 up over 10%, and the valuation is near all-time lows at a 9.3x forward P/E against analyst expectations of EPS growth over 27% a year. His base case is improving fundamentals: Pinterest is one of the few social platforms still adding North American users, who carry the highest advertising revenue per user, its users skew young so revenue per user should rise as they age, and operating margin is 6.3% and improving even after stock-based compensation. On timing, he suggests risk-neutral buyers put 75% of their intended allocation in before the print and 25% after, and risk-averse buyers split 50/50; Meta's strong advertising results are a positive read-across. The bear case is execution: research and development runs at over 29% of revenue — higher than Meta, Snap and Reddit — with little product innovation to show for it, and revenue per employee has fallen from its roughly $900,000 peak in 2022.

83F2533_VzU.title: Tesla Is Investing Aggressively in its Next Generation Technology | TSLA Stock Analysis
83F2533_VzU.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
83F2533_VzU.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc downgrades Tesla back to a SELL, reversing the HOLD stance he adopted when the shares fell to $300 earlier in 2026, where he closed his puts and short position for a profit. At about $379 (stated), the stock trades on 175x forward earnings against his $113 DCF fair value — roughly 70% downside over 12–18 months — and he says he is tempted to buy put options again, more so near $400. His base case rests on a weak third quarter: revenue flat at $28 billion year on year, EPS down 44%, automotive revenue down 3% to $20.5 billion, energy revenue down 16%, and operating income down 56%; he raised near-term DCF estimates only because 2026 capital spending was cut from $25 billion to $20 billion. The bull points he concedes are real: Full Self-Driving subscriptions up 67% to 1.74 million at about $99 a month, services and other revenue up to $4.6 billion, Tesla Semi volume production started, four new European FSD approvals, and about 1,000 robotaxis testing in Austin. The bear case is valuation and competition: the price assumes robotaxis and robots are inevitable, Chinese EV makers are eroding share in every contested region, and EV volumes have likely peaked near two million a year.

pW0cr707XPw.title: Meta Reveals Hardware Strategy to Investors
pW0cr707XPw.creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
pW0cr707XPw.summary: Parkevtate Vosianc walks through Meta's hardware strategy in a news-and-analysis update with no explicit buy or sell call and no valuation — the call is recorded as UNCERTAIN. The strategy he describes is to sell AI glasses close to cost, around $500, and monetise them through a Meta Muse subscription at about $9.99 a month, which he estimates could carry roughly 70% gross margins as recurring revenue; wearables are an open category with no dominant player, unlike phones against Apple. He says he likes the evidence that the spending is working: Meta AI engagement per person has more than doubled since April, and the Muse personal agent passed 10 million downloads in about six weeks. On the financial side, he thinks Reality Labs losses have peaked and should improve as spending shifts from virtual reality to AI, puts 2026 capital spending at at least $135 billion on revised estimates, and expects 2027 capex to rise further to $150–175 billion — spending investors will only accept if the engagement and revenue evidence keeps coming. No price or DCF figure is stated in this video.
